{"result": {"title": "People We Meet on Vacation", "author": "Emily Henry", "year": 2021, "word_count": 94000, "text": "Chapter 1.

Alex and I have taken a summer trip together every year since the year we met. This is not something we decided. It is something that happened to us, the way some habits do, so gradually that by the time you notice you have one, you are already attached to it and a little afraid to let it go.

The first trip was not really a trip. It was the drive home from college at the end of our junior year. We had met six weeks earlier in a poetry class neither of us had wanted to take, and by mid-April it was clear we could not live without one another's company for an entire summer. He was going home to East Linfield, Ohio. I was going home to Palmetto, Florida. We pulled up a map and drew the straightest possible line between the two towns, and then we crossed it out and drew a much crookeder line, because the first one went nowhere interesting.

Alex drove. Alex always drove. I did the playlists and the snacks and the terrible jokes. Somewhere in a gas-station parking lot in western North Carolina, at three in the morning, I discovered that he had been laughing politely at me for six hours and finally, finally, made him actually laugh. He has a specific laugh that he only lets out when he is genuinely amused, a short, quiet, surprised laugh that begins with a pulled-in breath. It is the single most rewarding sound in the world. I have been chasing it ever since.

That was nine summers ago. This year, for the first time, we were not going to take a trip. We hadn't spoken in almost two years. I had not told anyone I knew that I was flying to meet him, because if I had said it out loud, anyone I knew would have asked me whether I was sure this was a good idea, and I was not.", "source": "library-service"}, "error": null}
